FINAL SUBMISSION

What I submitted: the starting weights, unchanged (`/work/edited` contains no tensors, so the edited model equals the given weights, i.e., Qwen3.5-0.8B + the one listed earlier edit). My measured score difference is 0.0, rather than a possibly harmful nonzero edit.

What I changed and why: no weight tensors are edited by me. I investigated exhaustively and every candidate edit either collapsed accuracy on paired practice generations or was neutral-to-noisy. Submitting nothing is the choice my measurements support.

Evidence for that decision:
- Diagnosis of the failure mode (all measurements from teacher-forced passes on the given model): on the starting weights, 28.5% of generations run to the 8,192-token limit and are never correct; ~⅔ of those are degenerate tails where the model re-emits `</think>` every two tokens forever. The `</think>` logit is ~95% produced by layer-23 attention (writing ~21–31 along the `(1+γ)·E[</think>]` readout at essentially every position); embeddings and layers 0–22 contribute only a few points. There is no linearly separable "spam vs healthy close" direction in layer-23′s attention output (cosine with r(</think>) ≈ 0.29–0.43 in both regimes; the one-vs-other MLP difference direction is a small-sample artifact that generalizes badly).
- Edit 1 (difference-of-means rank-one pushing `</think>` down in spam, all 24 MLP down_projs, coefficient 0.2): −17.97 pp on 128 select problems (SE 4.63; 8 wrong→right vs 31 right→wrong); no-boxed rate 39→57%. Abandoned.
- Edit 2 (same construction, suppressing after any first close, coefficient 1.0): catastrophic — 98.4% of generations truncated, 0.0% accuracy. The direction fires in ordinary thinking sections and kills the close mechanism (the model had essentially no terminating behavior left). Abandoned.
- Edit 3 (ablate layer-23 down_proj columns 43/77/66, the units ~3–7× more active at spam positions): paired on 128 select-math problems −2.34 pp (SE 3.41); same edit on the second 128 (64 math + 64 GSM8K) +1.56 pp (SE 4.29). Truncation share fell consistently (32.8→25.0% and 22.7→14.1%) and no-boxed share fell (39→29% and 26→16%), but accuracy across all 256 select problems was net ≈ −0.4 pp — within standard error of zero, and on the MATH-500-like half, slightly negative. Columns {43,77} alone: exactly 0.0 pp.
- Per the task's own bar (an edit is kept only if its gain clearly exceeds its standard error on problems not used to choose it), no candidate qualifies; all promising directions were dose-response tested via paired "both" runs and judged harmful or neutral.

Why the original edit stands and nothing more: the earlier `W += 0.08·outer(u_</think>, b_loop)` is load-bearing — weakening it (or interacting edits pushing the same logit) removes the only mechanism that ends thinking and zeroes accuracy; strengthening or broadening it in my tests produced the same restart-`</think>` cascade it was designed to break. The remaining failure class (restarting the solution until the token limit) appears to require improved reasoning, which weight-space rank-one/ablation edits offered me could not produce without removing the termination mechanism entirely.

Strength of this submission: accuracy should equal the original weights on unseen problems (expected diff 0.0). I prefer that certain zero to the −2 to −18 pp losses measured for the tested edits, and I explicitly rejected the tempting "fewer truncations" metric because it did not convert into correct answers.
